rationale.usefulness: The README and getting-started archive document a coherent import, retrieve, draft, review and editable-export workflow for individual teachers. Recovery instructions and a teacher-scored evaluation protocol make a bounded trial actionable. Python operation, model configuration and unmeasured correction effort constrain broader accessibility; no generated artifact was inspected.
rationale.impact: Editable lesson bundles, provider choice and resumable phases could improve a defined preparation workflow. The evidence remains an existing single-teacher beta with synthetic/mocked software tests, no measured classroom benefit and no established wider adoption. It is a potentially useful domain application rather than demonstrated substantial progress in AI development.
rationale.novelty: The combination of curriculum retrieval, teaching-style context, editable bundles and saved generation phases is meaningfully tailored to teaching. The archives do not show that these components or orchestration methods are new relative to alternatives, nor provide controlled comparative outcomes. Differentiation is mostly workflow integration.
rationale.maturity: Documentation specifies Python requirements, worker operation, recovery thresholds, authentication boundaries and known experimental areas. However, this is explicitly beta and single-teacher, exports and provider behavior can vary, and no installation, live generation, interruption test or classroom assessment was performed. Synthetic tests cannot establish dependable pedagogical output.
rationale.openness: The original code has a supplied MIT license, documented local operation, multiple provider adapters and editable DOCX/PPTX outputs. These offer strong inspectability, adaptation and portability. Model weights/access, provider charges and third-party terms remain separate, and a fully local deployment still requires deliberate inference and network choices.
